4. Heard Sri Y.Ashok Raj, learned counsel for the petitioner and Ms.S.Madhavi, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor appearing for respondent No.1-State.
Despite notice, there is no representation on behalf of unofficial respondent No.2.

For the sake of convenience, the facts in Criminal Petition No.2552 of 2019 are discussed as hereunder:-
5.

On 23.07.2024, learned counsel for unofficial respondent No.1 submitted that the relief sought in this Criminal Petition does not survive as the subject matter of the case is transferred to other competent criminal Court.
But today, there is no representation on behalf of respondent No.1.
6. The brief facts of the case are that respondent No.2/complainant is doing real-estate business under the name and style of M/s.Vijayadurga Real Estates.
He along with one E.Satyanarayana Reddy purchased the plots situated at Thattiannaram Village, Saroornagar Mandal, Ranga Reddy District and sold them to the customers.

The petitioner/accused approached the complainant through his relative by name Sri P.Yadagiri and offered to sell the land admeasuring Ac.1.28 gts in survey No.137 of Lalgadi Malakpet Village, Shameerpet Mandal, for a total sale consideration of Rs.68,00,000/- and that on 13.08.2010, he paid Rs.38,00,000/- towards part sale consideration Mamindla Ashok vs The State Of Telangana on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4092298/
1 under agreement of sale dated 13.08.2010 to the petitioner in the presence of attesting witnesses namely, P.Yadagiri, Raju Goud and Ramesh.

sentences.text:
The accused sold another property i.e., an extent of land admeasuring Ac.1.00 gts in survey No.863 of Lalgadi Malakpet Village, Shameerpet Mandal,
Ranga Reddy District for a total sale consideration of Rs.20,00,000/- and that respondent No.2 paid Rs.10,00,000/- towards part sale consideration under the agreement of sale dated 13.08.2010 to which P.Yadagiri, Raju Goud and Ramesh are attesting witnesses and that the wife of the petitioner sold the plot admeasuring 400 sq.yrds in survey No.452 of Lalgadi Malakpet Village,
Shameerpet Mandal, Ranga Reddy District for a total sale consideration of Rs.29,50,000/- i.e., @
Rs.7,375/- per sq yrd and that he had paid Rs.19,50,000/- under agreement of sale dated 01.10.2010 executed by the wife of the petitioner to which B.Raju Goud and B.Ramesh stood as attesting witnesses and that again on 10.07.2013, paid Rs.10,00,000/- to the wife of the petitioner under a receipt.
7.

It is stated that on payment of advance money the petitioner showed the original documents and gave Encumbrance Certificate, Pahanies and Xerox copies of registered Gift Deed and Sale deeds but failed to give patta pass books and title deeds to respondent No.2, on the pretext of keeping the same as security with I.D.B.I. Bank, Basheerbagh Branch, Hyderabad.

On repeated requests, the petitioner and his wife refused to register the properties in favour of respondent No.2 which ended in cancellation of agreement of sale in respect of the above three properties.

8. It is further stated that the petitioner gave cheque bearing No.656136 dated 01.07.2014,
No.656137 dated 05.07.2014 for Rs.10,00,000/- and Rs.5,00,000/- respectively drawn on the State Bank of Hyderabad, Hakeempet Branch, Shameerpet Mandal, Ranga Reddy District towards refund of part sale consideration to him and the said cheques, on presentation were dishonoured for the reason "insufficient funds" on 10.09.2014 and that the Cheque bearing No.437592 dated 10.05.2014 of I.D.B.I. Bank, Basheerbagh Branch, Hyderabad issued for Rs.9,50,000/- given by the wife of the petitioner, was returned dishonoured on 22.07.2014 for the reason payment stopped.
9.
It is further submitted that respondent No.2/complainant along with one Yadullah Hussain and Srikanth Reddy forced the petitioner to pay the money.

Hence, the petitioner executed promissory notes for Rs.58,00,000/- in favour of respondent No.2 to which P.Ramesh, Raju Goud and J.
Mahesh stood as the attesting witnesses and that the wife of the petitioner executed promissory notes for Rs.19,50,000/- on 16.02.2016, in favour of respondent No.2, to which Raju Goud and J.Mahesh stood as the attesting witnesses.
It is stated that both the promissory notes were handed over to respondent No.2 on 09.10.2014 but remained unpaid.

Respondent No.2 along with G.Naresh and J.Mahender approached the petitioner and his wife on 12.04.2015 and 15.10.2015 and demanded Rs.77,50,000/- by virtue of promissory notes dated 16.02.2016 but the accused and his wife sought time to pay the money.

On repeated demands, the accused issued cheque bearing No.565210, dated 25.06.2018 for Rs.48,00,000/-, cheque Nos.656134 and 656135 dated 25.06.2018 of Rs.4,00,000/- each drawn on the State Bank of Hyderabad, Hakeempet Branch, Shameerpet Mandal, Ranga Reddy District and the accused and his wife gave two cheques bearing Nos.437590 and 437591 dated 25.06.2018 for Rs.4,00,000/- each drawn on I.D.B.I. Bank, Basheerbagh Branch,
Hyderabad.
On presentation, these cheques were returned dishonoured for the reason refer to drawer and payment stopped on 10.08.2018 and 07.07.2018.

Then, respondent No.2 filed private Mamindla Ashok vs The State Of Telangana on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4092298/
2 complaint under Section 200 of Cr.P.C. for the offences punishable under Sections 406 and 420 of I.P.C. before the learned XI Metropolitan Magistrate Court, Ranga Reddy District which is referred for investigation under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C. which is registered as Crime No.256 of 2018 against the petitioner and his wife and the same is pending.

sentences.text: 10. It is contended that respondent No.2 issued legal notice to the petitioner on 07.09.2018 and 24.09.2018 under Section 138(b) of the Negotiable Instruments Act (for short, "the NI Act").
The accused replied the same but failed to pay the money due.
Hence, respondent No.2 filed the present complaint against the petitioner vide C.C.No.99 of 2019 for the offence punishable under Section 138 of the NI Act.
11. Learned counsel for the petitioner contended that the petitioner and respondent No.2 were acquainted with each other.
Out of such an acquaintance, he approached respondent No.2 for a hand loan of Rs.10,00,000/- to meet his family needs.

On such request, respondent No.2 paid Rs.10,00,000/- to him by obtaining petitioner's signatures on blank signed promissory notes, blank cheques, blank stamp papers etc and obtained two registered gift settlement deeds bearing Nos.7778/2005 dated 18.11.2005, No.47/2010 dated 16.01.2010 pertaining to agricultural land admeasuring Ac1.28 gts, forming part of land in survey No.137 and land admeasuring Ac1.00 gts in survey No.863 of Lalgadi Malakpet Village and Grampanchayath, Shamirpet Mandal of Ranga Reddy District and with regard to the open plot admeasuring 400 sq. yrds in survey No.542 of the same Village and District, standing in the name of the wife of the petitioner.

He submitted that respondent No.2 also took original patta pass books and title deeds of the agricultural land as a collateral security and promised to return all these documents on receipt of the loan amount.
12. Learned counsel for the petitioner further submitted that the petitioner repaid the entire loan amount along with interest which came to Rs.22,00,000/-.
Having received the loan amount from the petitioner, respondent No.2 failed to return the documents placed as collateral security.
After a lapse of many years, he fabricated the documents and cooked up a false story and invented the C.C.No.99 of 2019 for extorting money from the petitioner.

13. Learned counsel for the petitioner further contended that respondent No.2, instead of returning the documents to the petitioner, threatened him with dire consequences to extract huge sum of money illegally and demanded him to pay Rs.60,00,000/-.

When the petitioner refused to pay money, respondent No.2 accompanied with anti-social elements, came to the petitioner with knives,
daggers and sticks.
The petitioner raised hue and cry and then, the local villagers came to rescue the petitioner, due to which, respondent No.2 ran away.

It is stated that, unable to bear the illegal activities of respondent No.2, the petitioner lodged a complaint against respondent No.2 vide Crime No.256 of 2018 for the offences under Sections 386, 406, 420, 423, 424, 506 r/w Section 34 of I.P.C., which pending adjudication.

As counter blast to the said Crime No.256 of 2018, respondent No.2 invented the false proceedings against the petitioner, vide C.C.No.99 of 2019 before the trial Court, under Sections 138 and 142 of the NI Act.
Therefore, he seeks to quash the impugned proceedings.

sentences.text: Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor submitted that the matter requires to be tried and seeks to dismiss the Criminal Petition.

15. Having regard to the submissions made by both the learned counsel, this Court is of the opinion that the matter requires full-fledged trial and only upon completion of trial, the truth would come to light.
However, the appearance of the petitioner before the trial Court is dispensed with on all occasions, unless and until required by it.
The trial Court is directed to conduct the trial without being influenced by any of the observations made in this order.
The petitioner is granted liberty to work out the remedies available under law.
16. With the above direction, these Criminal Petition Nos.2552, 2553 and 2561 of 2019 are disposed of.
Miscellaneous Petitions, pending if any, shall stand closed.
